bias_direction: The same session that removed the R7 floor from the enforcer is attesting that recording the removal in this DR was done faithfully. The pull is toward describing the floor's removal as pure correction rather than as what it also is, a weakening of a gate the next batch is judged by: the DR callout and the contract resolution could have presented batch 23's gaming of the floor as the whole story and left out that nothing now checks candidate volume at all. The callout names the two remaining enforcers so a reader can test whether they actually cover what the floor claimed to.
independent_reviewer_counterclaim: A reviewer could hold that a floor which batch 23 gamed should have been hardened, not removed: a ratio over byte-rooted candidates (RC1's surfaced_in) instead of typed counts would keep a numeric check while closing the gaming route, and removing it leaves R7 asserting only arithmetic consistency, which a session can satisfy by logging any self-consistent counts. Against that: the plan's argument is that any floor on candidate volume still rewards staging for its own sake, which batch 23 showed, and the arithmetic check is kept because it is the one part of the log the party being judged cannot make true by adding rows; whether that trade is right is for the owner in the PR.
